newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BROTEN SHOT OFF GOALIE GIVES DALLAS OT WIN IN LAST MINUTE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BROTEN SHOT OFF GOALIE GIVES DALLAS OT WIN IN LAST MINUTE.

text.p: Neal Broten banked a backhander off goaltender Stephane Fiset from behind the net with 43 seconds left in overtime to give the Dallas Stars a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings Sunday.

Derian Hatcher flipped a shot from a few feet inside the Los Angeles blue line and Fiset kicked it aside with his left pad. But Broten got the rebound and backhanded it into the net off the goalie's mask for his third goal of the season and third in five games with the Stars.

"It wasn't just my goal. All five guys contributed to that winning goal," Broten said. "I won the faceoff, but Hatcher did a great job of getting the shot off and everybody else did a great job of tying up a player. I just happened to find myself alone by the goal."
Broten had no goals in 18 games for the Kings before they waived him at the end of last month.

"I'm really beginning to feel confident now," he said. "I like the guys on this team and I feel very comfortable playing with them. Los Angeles did me a favour by sending me back here. This is where my family is and I love coming to the rink every day."

Pat Verbeek had the other tally for Dallas, which has won four straight at home, has won three of its last four games overall and is 7-3-1 in its last 11. The Stars, playing their fourth game in five nights, moved within four points of idle Colorado for first place in the Western Conference.
"For not having anything in the tank, we really hung together," said Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock.

Kevin Stevens got the only goal for Los Angeles, which has lost three of four. The Kings were playing without injured regulars Dimitri Khristich and Yanic Perreault and suspended defenceman Rob Blake.

"We gave a real good effort, despite the fact we were missing a lot of guys tonight," Fiset said. "I feel our effort warranted at least a tie. I did my best to keep the team in the game and I feel as though I did do my job."
Fiset made 29 saves, while Andy Moog stopped 26 shots.

At Florida, Rob Niedermayer scored a power-play goal and set up another in a three-goal first period and the Panthers held on for a 4-3 victory over the New York Rangers, ending their four-game winless streak.

Scott Mellanby and Martin Straka also scored in the first period for the Panthers, who are unbeaten in eight of their last nine games (5-1-3) and took the season series from New York, 3-1-2. Jody Hull scored the other Florida goal.

"The Rangers are a big rival, we're always up for them," said Niedermayer. "I'm kind of sorry our season series is over, but they'll be around during the playoffs and so will we. Maybe we'll get them again."

Adam Graves scored on a deflection with 2:36 remaining in regulation to lift the Rangers within 4-3, but New York was unable to muster another solid scoring chance and had its four-game road winning streak snapped.
New York's Wayne Gretzky had an assist but his goal-scoring drought extended to a career-high 17 games.
In Buffalo, Dominik Hasek continued his stellar play with 32 saves and Jason Dawe and Derek Plante scored as the Sabres edged the Ottawa Senators 2-1, extending their unbeaten streak to seven games.
Buffalo, which moved back ahead of Pittsburgh atop the Northeast Division, is 4-0-3 in its last seven games and 3-0-2 in its last five at home.
The Senators had their franchise-record four-game unbeaten streak snapped and fell to 4-2-3 in their last nine games.
In his last seven games, Hasek has posted a 4-0-3 record, giving up just eight goals on 213 shots for a gaudy .962 save percentage.
In Calgary, Robert Reichel and Jarome Iginla scored 33 seconds apart late in the first period and Dave Gagner tallied twice as the Flames cruised to a 6-1 victory over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
Jonas Hoglund and Mike Sullivan also scored for the Flames. Theo Fleury assisted on three of the goals and Trevor Kidd stopped 24 shots.
Teemu Selanne accounted for Anaheim's offence, scoring a goal for the third straight game.
In Edmonton, Ryan Smyth and Mariusz Czerkawski each had a goal and an assist to lead the surging Oilers to a 4-1 victory over the Washington Capitals.
Bob Essensa made 30 saves for for Edmonton, which has won six of its last seven games overall and at home.
Jaroslav Svejkovsky netted the lone goal, his second in as many games, for Washington, which fell to 1-2-1 on its five-game road trip.
